title: a-shim-status-pane-carries-a-pid
intention: Every device's shim status pane carries its PID, answering 'am I running, and as what' uniformly across devices.
why: The generalization of the parent: every device answers 'am I running, and as what' the same way.
traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured: 'am I running' is a measurement
Law 10 — nothing in the system is immeasurable: PID + liveness is the instrument

falsifier.proves_red: The pane shows a pid that is not the device's own process — the failure this ticket is being held to avoid.

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: [ABSORBED] by every-device-has-a-presence child (b) — pid only meaningful once devices are separate OS processes, which is what that parent ticket builds
watchme: none, because it rests at THINKME; the watch question is answered when it is cast forward.
intent: Process id becomes part of the BaseShim device status pane generally, not just the ground loop's.
HELD_AT_THINKME_ON_PURPOSE: This one is NOT ready and is cast resting at THINKME rather than BUILDME. A shim's pid is only meaningful once devices are separate OS processes — which is exactly what Akien's ruling enables (the loop scans disk and posts to the bus, so the heartbeat no longer holds in-process references) but which is NOT yet built. Today every shim shares the pid of whatever process constructed it, so a pid field would report a true number that means nothing. Casting it at BUILDME would invite building a field that is honest-looking and empty.
stage_needs_retired: ABSORBED 2026-08-11 — needs transferred to parent every-device-has-a-presence child (b); the stage they referenced (BUILDME) is not in this absorbed ticket's vocabulary

absorbed_by.why: This ticket's recorded why — 'every device answers am I running, and as what, the same way' — IS that child. The parent generalizes it: the answer is three states (never-booted / running / offline-with-last-known), and the pid becomes a FIELD of the running state rather than a pane element of its own. Absorbed rather than worked in parallel, so one question does not get two builds. The blocker recorded here in HELD_AT_THINKME_ON_PURPOSE is unchanged and is now the parent's first open question: a pid is only meaningful once devices are separate OS processes, and no shim spawns one yet.

retirement: ABSORBED — this ticket is child (b) of every-device-has-a-presence, which already carries the pid/presence requirement as part of its build design. The parent ticket has a concrete how block and is at BUILDME. Building this separately would duplicate work.
